      {"@context":"http://schema.org","@graph":[{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Kiwibank","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/kiwibank"},"datePublished":"2026-07-13T20:20:01.035Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/kiwibank_at-kiwibank-we-know-that-growth-looks-different-activity-7482529288550903808-woRA","text":"At Kiwibank, we know that growth looks different for everyone. \n\nWhether it's exploring a new career path, building confidence in your current role, expanding your network, or developing new skills, we're committed to creating opportunities that help our kaimahi grow in ways that are meaningful to them. \n\nThat's why our Women’s Network recently spearheaded a series of career connection events across the country, bringing people together for open, honest conversations about career mobility, mentorship, self-advocacy, influence, and navigating change. \n\nThere were no presentations or panels - just colleagues sharing experiences, challenges, insights, and practical advice. This scheme allows our people to pay for their public transport through a salary sacrifice deduction from their gross salary, which means, in effect, they pay less for their public transport. \n\nWhen we recently introduced the scheme through an internal learning session, more than 200 Kiwibank kaimahi joined to learn how it works and what the savings could look like. \n\nAnd it's easy to see why. \n\n👉 Spend $50 on eligible public transport and you could be around $18 better off, depending on your tax rate, your KiwiSaver contribution and your salary. \n\nNot by travelling less. Not by changing your habits. Simply by making your money work harder for you. \n\nOne of our early testers, Tim McBride, summed it up perfectly: \n💬 \"It's money I was going to spend anyway, so if I can save on it, why wouldn't I?\"\n\nFor us, this is more than just a new scheme we’re offering our people. It's another way we're helping our people keep more of their hard-earned money in their pockets. \n\nBecause helping Kiwi be better off starts with helping our own people be better off too. \n\nNgā mihi to Mary Miles and Steven Zinsli 💳 for leading the discussion and to the teams behind the scenes bringing this to life at Kiwibank. ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/kiwibank_what-if-you-could-save-money-on-your-commute-activity-7479999258100948993-QCU2"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Kiwibank","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/kiwibank"},"datePublished":"2026-07-02T22:29:13.523Z","headline":"Kiwibank | Business Online Call - July 2026","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/kiwibank_kiwibank-business-online-call-july-2026-activity-7478575538358530049-7Ac9","text":"A better return for Kiwi businesses. She’s a Business Support Specialist based in Ōtautahi Christchurch, bringing fresh perspectives and curiosity to our Enterprise Operations team.  \n\n“I first joined Kiwibank as an intern in 2024, before heading back to uni to finish my degree in Finance and Ecology. Along the way, I also completed a semester on exchange in Denmark - which was an amazing experience (the biking, landscapes, pastries and a good 2 months of amazing travel thrown in). \n\nComing back to Kiwibank in 2026 felt like an easy decision. I was keen to start my permanent career in the banking world, but it was really the people and the purpose that made me want to return. \n\nSince coming back, I’ve shifted from project work into real-world customer support - managing cases, improving processes, and working closely as a team to get the best outcomes for our customers. It’s been a big learning curve for sure, but a really rewarding one. No day is like the other, and that’s what keeps it interesting! \n\nMy role helps keep things running behind the scenes - supporting business customers with everything from onboarding and internet banking to term deposits and account support. It’s fast-paced, collaborative, and very solutions-focused, with everyone working together to problem-solve to make things easier for customers. \n\nI’ve loved being part of the small moments that help businesses achieve their goals - like setting up a term deposit. Even contributing in a small way feels meaningful when you know it’s helping a customer move forward. \n\nWhat’s stood out most is my team. Everyone is so supportive, welcoming, and always willing to help - it made the transition from intern to full-time feel really smooth. That’s when I knew, this is why I work here. \n\nLooking ahead, I want to keep learning - especially how the wider business connects and contributes to making Kiwi better off.     <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">At Kiwibank, we know that growth looks different for everyone. 

Whether it's exploring a new career path, building confidence in your current role, expanding your network, or developing new skills, we're committed to creating opportunities that help our kaimahi grow in ways that are meaningful to them. 

That's why our Women’s Network recently spearheaded a series of career connection events across the country, bringing people together for open, honest conversations about career mobility, mentorship, self-advocacy, influence, and navigating change. 

There were no presentations or panels - just colleagues sharing experiences, challenges, insights, and practical advice. The aim was simple: for everyone to leave with at least one new connection that supports their growth and confidence. 

As our Women’s Network Co-Chair <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/chloegunn?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Chloe Gunn</a> puts it: 

“The magic happens when women (and everyone!) realise they're not figuring it all out alone. Creating space to openly share experiences, challenges and ambitions helps build confidence, connection, and reminds us that there are so many different ways to build a meaningful career.” 

This kōrero was a powerful reminder that there’s no single path to success - and that some of the best opportunities for growth come from learning from each other👏 </p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">What if you could save money on your commute without changing how you travel? 🚌💸 At Kiwibank, we're constantly looking for practical ways to help our kaimahi be better off. 

That's why we've introduced a new public transport scheme through <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/extraordinarypay?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Extraordinary</a>, helping our people save money to get to and from work. This scheme allows our people to pay for their public transport through a salary sacrifice deduction from their gross salary, which means, in effect, they pay less for their public transport. 

When we recently introduced the scheme through an internal learning session, more than 200 Kiwibank kaimahi joined to learn how it works and what the savings could look like. 

And it's easy to see why. 

👉 Spend $50 on eligible public transport and you could be around $18 better off, depending on your tax rate, your KiwiSaver contribution and your salary. 

Not by travelling less. Not by changing your habits. Simply by making your money work harder for you. 

One of our early testers, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/timmcbride91?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Tim McBride</a>, summed it up perfectly: 
💬 "It's money I was going to spend anyway, so if I can save on it, why wouldn't I?"

For us, this is more than just a new scheme we’re offering our people. It's another way we're helping our people keep more of their hard-earned money in their pockets. 

Because helping Kiwi be better off starts with helping our own people be better off too. 

Ngā mihi to <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/maryspence?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Mary Miles</a> and <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/steven-zinsli-%F0%9F%92%B3-aa813184?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Steven Zinsli 💳</a> for leading the discussion and to the teams behind the scenes bringing this to life at Kiwibank. </p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Moving with purpose, together 🌈💚

For the third year running, our kaimahi have proudly taken part in Sweat with Pride, joining colleagues from across the banking sector in a strong display of industry-wide allyship for our Rainbow communities.
 
Throughout June, teams from <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/showcase/anznewzealand/?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>ANZ Aotearoa</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/asb-bank?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>ASB Bank</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/bankofnewzealand?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Bank of New Zealand</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/westpac-new-zealand-limited?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Westpac New Zealand</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/tsb_nz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>TSB New Zealand</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/the-co-operative-bank?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>The Co-operative Bank</a> and <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/kiwibank?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Kiwibank</a> came together to hīkoi across the motu. These events offered an opportunity to connect, celebrate Pride Month and demonstrate our collective commitment to inclusion.
 
These walks are about more than movement; they're about backing organisations that make a real difference in the lives of Rainbow and Takatāpui communities. Funds raised during this month support the work of <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/burnettfoundation?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Burnett Foundation Aotearoa</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/rainbow-youth?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>RainbowYOUTH</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/outlineaotearoa?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>OutLine Aotearoa</a> and <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/insideoutkoaro?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>InsideOUT Kōaro</a>, helping to provide advocacy, education, counselling, peer support and safe spaces for people across the motu.
 
They’re a shared commitment to inclusion and to making all Kiwi better off. We’re proud to stand alongside a sector that uplifts and celebrates our Rainbow and Takatāpui whānau.
 
It’s something we’re proud to be part of - an industry that turns intent into action. Take a look at the highlights from Wellington, Dunedin and Auckland ⬇

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">We’re celebrating the kaimahi who bring Kiwibank to life across Aotearoa – sharing their stories, passions and mahi 👋💚 Say Kia ora to <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/laurabeagley?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Laura Beagley</a>. She’s a Business Support Specialist based in Ōtautahi Christchurch, bringing fresh perspectives and curiosity to our Enterprise Operations team.  

“I first joined Kiwibank as an intern in 2024, before heading back to uni to finish my degree in Finance and Ecology. Along the way, I also completed a semester on exchange in Denmark - which was an amazing experience (the biking, landscapes, pastries and a good 2 months of amazing travel thrown in). 

Coming back to Kiwibank in 2026 felt like an easy decision. I was keen to start my permanent career in the banking world, but it was really the people and the purpose that made me want to return. 

Since coming back, I’ve shifted from project work into real-world customer support - managing cases, improving processes, and working closely as a team to get the best outcomes for our customers. It’s been a big learning curve for sure, but a really rewarding one. No day is like the other, and that’s what keeps it interesting! 

My role helps keep things running behind the scenes - supporting business customers with everything from onboarding and internet banking to term deposits and account support. It’s fast-paced, collaborative, and very solutions-focused, with everyone working together to problem-solve to make things easier for customers. 

I’ve loved being part of the small moments that help businesses achieve their goals - like setting up a term deposit. Even contributing in a small way feels meaningful when you know it’s helping a customer move forward. 

What’s stood out most is my team. Everyone is so supportive, welcoming, and always willing to help - it made the transition from intern to full-time feel really smooth. That’s when I knew, this is why I work here. 

Looking ahead, I want to keep learning - especially how the wider business connects and contributes to making Kiwi better off. There are so many opportunities here, and I’m excited to see where I can grow next. 

If there’s one piece of advice I’d give? Give it a go - take every opportunity, say yes, and learn as much as you can!”</p>
